# orchestrator

A Claude Code skill that turns your main session into a dispatcher that never blocks.

Every task goes to a background subagent. The main session only plans, dispatches, tracks
and reports, so you can keep talking while 3-5 agents work. A small ledger file
(`.claude/orchestrator.md`) tracks every agent and survives context compaction.

## Install

```bash
npx skills add olivieropinotti/orchestrator-skill
```

Then type `/orchestrator` in Claude Code. Say "stop orchestrating" to turn it off.

## What it does

- Splits each message into independent tasks and dispatches them in parallel.
- Sends follow-ups to the agent already on that topic, so its context stays intact.
- Writes a full brief for every agent: goal, facts, files it owns, what it must not do,
  and what "done" means.
- Picks the model per task: Opus for judgment, Sonnet for tight, checkable tasks.
- Answers "status" from the ledger.

## Commands

- `status`: list every agent and its state
- `stop ` / `stop all`
- `redirect  to ...`

MIT licensed.

# be-ambitious

A free Claude skill that makes your agent more ambitious when you invoke it.

It turns Felix Rieseberg's article [How to be more ambitious: a tutorial for humans with models](https://felixrieseberg.com/how-to-be-more-ambitious-a-tutorial-for-humans-with-models/) into steps an agent follows. Felix works on Claude at Anthropic. All the ideas are his.

## What it does

Most of us use a model at the size of the task we typed. Felix's point: the model can do far more if you aim it higher, deeper or wider. He names four types of ambition. The skill uses three of them:

| Type | The question it asks | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Altitude** | What's the goal beyond the goal? | Don't fix one crash. Keep the app crash-free. |
| **Depth** | What would the best expert in the field do, from the raw data, and what outside check proves it's right? | Don't make a markdown table. Load the data into a database and fit a real statistical model. |
| **Range** | Which other fields would help, and what do their experts actually do? | Bring in a journalist, an editor and a short seller, and have each do their real job. |

The fourth type, **Speed** (the same work in less time), is how most people already use AI, so Felix skips it and so does the skill.

When you invoke it, the skill:

1. Finds the goal beyond the goal.
2. Picks the types that fit your task (usually one or two, not all three).
3. Writes the ambitious plan: a 3-rung ladder for Altitude, Felix's four expert questions for Depth, and the crew for Range.
4. Lists the data, tools and access the plan needs, and what's missing.
5. Rewrites your prompt at that level, ending with an outside check and what counts as a pass.
6. Does the work, if you handed it a task. Stops after the rewrite, if you handed it a prompt to improve.

# Solid Glass

[The style](#the-style) · [Install](#install) · [What is here](#what-is-here) · [Contributing](#contributing)

A refined glass-inspired aesthetic that feels solid from afar and reveals its subtle materiality up
close. Delicate highlights, fine borders, and soft shadows create depth, while a restrained finish
emphasizes clarity, stability, and a sense of solidity over transparency, refraction, and fluidity.

That is one of the [blocks](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/blocks): whole screens made of the
components, to look at, read and copy in. Below, the components themselves.

It stands between flat design and liquid glass. Flat is an opaque block with no finish to speak of;
liquid glass is nearly clear, and on a page with a lot of text the reader is always fighting the
background for the words. Solid Glass lets only an outline through: enough to know it is glass, not
enough to get in the way of reading.

## The style

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tactility** | Interfaces that feel tangible. Every interaction carries a subtle sense of touch and response. |
| **Precision** | Clean geometry, refined details, and restrained lighting create a precise, technical aesthetic. |
| **Physicality** | Depth comes from thickness, shadow, and spatial hierarchy, giving every element a sense of physical presence. |

AI applications are built around information that is constantly changing — responses streaming in,

Solid Glass keeps the interface calm and readable. Neutral surfaces reduce visual distractions,
depth establishes hierarchy, and color and motion are reserved for meaningful feedback.

---

## 三件事

### 从零生成

给它一个题目、一篇文章、一份口播稿或大纲，它先写出结论式标题和口播备注，再排版、配图、加动画。

### 照参考图美化

给它一份朴素的 .pptx 和一张参考图，它把原文一字不改地搬进统一的配色、版式、图标和插画里，少一个字都不交。

### 原生可编辑

文字是文本框，表格是真表格，图表是 PowerPoint 原生图表，双击就能改数据。PowerPoint、WPS、Keynote 都能打开。

---

## 效果示例

### 同一页内容，美化前后

左边是原稿，右边是换上暖橙风格之后的样子。标题和数字一个没动，柱状图还是能改数据的原生图表。

### 文字一个不动，换身衣服

上面一排是原稿，下面一排是给了一张薄荷绿参考图之后美化出来的。标题、要点、数字一个字都没改，换掉的是配色、版式、图标和插画。

### 同一份原稿，换一张参考图就是另一套风格

从上往下依次是原稿、薄荷参考图、深色科技、墨水杂志。四个版本文字完全一样。

### 参考图里有什么，封面就画什么

参考图是一张环保科普封面，山坡上立着风车。美化后的封面照着参考图的元素画出了风景，整张图没接任何 AI 生图模型，是程序画出来的。

### 理科课件，公式一个不丢

一份高中数学导数复习课，原稿里有 12 个用公式编辑器打的公式，在 LibreOffice 里打开全是空白。解析时它会把这类公式转成普通文字公式，换什么软件都看得到，也能直接改字。

### 一篇文章，直接变成能讲的 PPT

把一篇公众号文章丢给它，生成 15 页的口播 PPT。它先写一份只有标题的"幽灵稿"让你确认，每页标题都是一句结论，每页都带口播备注。

### 数据、流程、分析框架也装得下

时间线、漏斗、中心辐射、2x2 矩阵、原生表格、原生图表，外加 SWOT、PEST、波特五力、商业画布。表格是真表格，图表双击就能改数据。

### 工具教程的截图有专门的版式

一张截图配几条说明，说明里写上位置，截图上就打一个对应的编号点。几张截图走一个流程，按各自的宽高比分配宽度，中间自动加箭头。

---

## 它解决什么

AI 做的 PPT，常见的毛病就这几样。

- 整页是一张图片，看着漂亮，错一个字也改不了
- 能编辑的又是一股模板味，谁做出来都长一个样
- 内容装不下就把字越缩越小，投到墙上看不清

ingestr is a command-line app that allows you to ingest data from any source into any destination using simple command-line flags, no code necessary.

You can install `ingestr` using the install script:

```sh
curl -LsSf https://getbruin.com/install/ingestr | sh
```

Alternatively, you can install it with pip:

```sh
pip install ingestr
```

The pip package can also be used from Python. Install the SDK extra for Python data ingestion:

```sh
pip install 'ingestr[sdk]'
```

Python rows, generators, and DataFrames are sent to the `ingestr` CLI binary as Arrow IPC streams by default. The pip package downloads and caches the matching GitHub release binary on first use:

```python
import ingestr

ingestr.ingest(
    [{"id": 1, "name": "Ada"}, {"id": 2, "name": "Grace"}],
    dest_uri="duckdb:///tmp/warehouse.duckdb",
    dest_table="main.people",
)
```

DataFrames and yielded data use the same Arrow stream transport:

```python
ingestr.ingest(df, dest_uri="duckdb:///tmp/warehouse.duckdb", dest_table="main.events")

def events():
    yield [{"id": 1, "event": "signup"}]
```

FluentCMS v2: a headless CMS built for AI agents to operate and for a team to govern
Created by Momentaj, a Toronto AI engineering firm.

> **Status: pre-alpha.** v2 is a rewrite from scratch, in progress on this branch. Nothing runs yet.
> The previous version lives on the [`dev` branch](https://github.com/FluentCMS/fluentcms/tree/dev) and receives security fixes only. There is no migration path from v1 to v2.

## What v2 is

The agent does the work by default. People write the rules and review what matters before it goes live.

- **Agents operate the CMS through [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).** Every capability is a tool before it is a screen. Forms are the fallback for people.
- **The rule book is enforced.** Rules are written in plain language and compiled into checks that block violations. A rule that cannot be checked is labelled advisory and shown as such.
- **Facts live once.** Prices, dates, names and limits are typed entities with a source and an owner. Content references them and never stores a copy.
- **Every change is a change set.** Grouped edits with a diff, the agent's rationale and its sources. Routine sets pass on checks, risky sets wait for a person, large sets are sampled. A set is published and reverted atomically.
- **Every published item carries provenance.** Was AI involved, who reviewed it, and where the facts came from.

Agents never approve or publish by judgment. Only checks can auto-publish, and only where a routing rule allows it.

Delivery is headless: frontends read a delivery API. There is no built-in renderer, theme or page builder.

cambios.descripcion: This plugin provides a specialized suite of skills for data engineers and database practitioners working on Google Cloud. It acts as an expert assistant, allowing you to use natural language prompts in your preferred coding agent to architect complex data pipelines, transform data with dbt, write Spark and BigQuery SQL notebooks, and orchestrate end-to-end workflows across GCP's data ecosystem.

Deploy, manage and monitor your Hostinger services directly from Claude Code. The plugin connects Claude to Hostinger's remote MCP server, so you can ship sites and apps, manage domains and DNS, run WordPress and operate VPS servers without leaving your coding environment. There's nothing to install on your machine: no Node.js, no npm, no local server. Key features include one-prompt deployments for static sites, Node.js apps (built on Hostinger), full WordPress site imports, and WordPress plugins and themes, plus static and PHP sites on the Agency Plan. Beyond deployments, Claude can search and register domains, edit DNS records and snapshots, check build logs, and manage mailboxes, online stores, email marketing contacts, subscriptions and orders. It can also control VPS firewalls, snapshots and monitoring. Sign in through your browser (OAuth) on first use, or set a `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` from hPanel. How to use: there are no commands to memorize. Describe what you want and Claude picks the right tool or deployment skill. Try "deploy my static site to Hostinger", "deploy this Next.js app to example.com", "create an A record pointing example.com to 1.2.3.4", or "show VPS metrics for the last 24 hours."

Security review for Claude-generated code. Pattern-based warnings on edits, LLM-powered diff review on Stop, and an agentic commit reviewer that catches injection, XSS, SSRF, hardcoded secrets, and 25+ other vulnerability classes.
